title: Relative and absolute pseudo-coherence agree for flat finitely presented space morphisms
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived tensor uses K-flat resolutions and $R\Gamma$ uses K-injective resolutions [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. A perfect object is etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Pseudo-coherent on a space means that etale locally on affine scheme charts the object is represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free structure modules; pseudo-coherent in $D(A)$ means quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above finite-free $A$-complex [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. For a locally finite type morphism $g:Z\to T$ of algebraic spaces, an object $L\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $T$ if for every integer $m$ and every commutative square $U\to V$, $U\to Z$, $V\to T$ with $U,V$ schemes and the vertical maps etale, $L|_U$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $V$. Here on scheme charts use [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]: locally factor $U\to V$ as a closed immersion into finite-dimensional affine space over $V$; its derived pushforward admits locally a strictly perfect approximation inducing cohomology isomorphisms above $m$ and a surjection in degree $m$. The affine covers, factorizations and approximations may depend on $m$. Let $S$ be a scheme, let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ which is flat and locally of finite presentation, and let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts. Then $K$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $Y$ if and only if $K$ is pseudo-coherent on $X$. No quasi-compactness, separatedness, properness or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Consider any presentation diagram $fa=bh$, with schemes $U,V$, etale $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$, and $h:U\to V$. Flatness and local finite presentation are etale local on source-and-target by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties]. Thus [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] makes $h$ flat and locally of finite presentation, and also supplies a presentation with $a$ surjective. These properties imply local finite type: on affines a finitely presented algebra is finitely generated. By [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus], $a^*K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology and is exact restriction to the slice site. The equivalence [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] therefore gives $E_U\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{Zar}})$ and its canonical identification $\epsilon_U^*E_U\cong a^*K$. This is the scheme object meant by $K|_U$ in the relative definition.

proof.text: For each such $h$, apply [lem-sfb-flat-ambient-relative-pseudocoherence] to $U\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_U}U\xrightarrow{h}V$ and $E_U$. The identity is a closed immersion: on each affine its ring map is the identity surjection with zero kernel. Its direct-image functor on module sheaves is the identity, so applying it to a K-injective resolution computes $R(\mathrm{id}_U)_*E_U\cong E_U$. Hence $E_U$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $V$ if and only if it is pseudo-coherent on the Zariski scheme $U$. The ambient lemma imposes no boundedness or quasi-compactness condition on $E_U$ or $U$.

proof.text: Suppose $K$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $Y$. In a presentation with $a:U\to X$ surjective, the definition gives relative $m$-pseudo-coherence of $E_U$ for every $m$, hence relative pseudo-coherence. Step 2 makes $E_U$ absolutely pseudo-coherent. By [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], it has bounded-above finite-free models on a Zariski open cover of $U$. The exact tensor pullback $\epsilon_U^*$ of [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] preserves quasi-isomorphisms and finite free structure modules, so these become etale-local models of $a^*K$. They give local models on every object $W\to X$ of the small etale site: [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] makes $W\times_XU\to W$ a surjective etale scheme cover; pull back the chosen open cover of $U$ to it. On these refinements, pullback is the exact slice restriction of [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus], so it preserves the models. To meet the chain-map form of [def-sfb-space-pseudocoherent-complex], represent $K$ by a K-injective complex $I$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex] on the small etale model. Its restriction to every object of the site is again K-injective [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], so each of the above derived-category isomorphisms $F\to I|_{W'}$ is the class of a chain map [lem-sc-kinjective-quasi-iso-comparison], which is then a quasi-isomorphism. Covering transitivity, applied to the sieves generated by these refinements, now gives exactly the local finite-free condition of [def-sfb-space-pseudocoherent-complex] on $X$ with $P=I$. No common upper bound is chosen.

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $K$ is pseudo-coherent on $X$. For an arbitrary presentation of step 1, restrict the local finite-free models in [def-sfb-space-pseudocoherent-complex] to the slice site of $U$. By the exact restriction of [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] they give local bounded-above finite-free models $P^\bullet$ of $a^*K$. For each integer $m$, the stupid truncation $P^{\ge m}\to P$ is a map from a bounded finite-free complex: it is the identity in degrees $\ge m$ and zero below. On cohomology it is an isomorphism above $m$, and in degree $m$ it is the quotient $\ker d^m\twoheadrightarrow\ker d^m/\operatorname{im}d^{m-1}$. Thus $a^*K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ for every $m$. By [lem-sfb-etale-pseudocoherence-descent], applied to $E_U$ and $\epsilon_U^*E_U\cong a^*K$ from step 1, $E_U$ is pseudo-coherent on $U_{\mathrm{Zar}}$. Step 2 makes it pseudo-coherent relative to $V$, hence relatively $m$-pseudo-coherent for every $m$ by [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Since the presentation was arbitrary, the quantified definition in the statement proves relative pseudo-coherence of $K$ over $Y$. The local models, refinements and truncations may depend on $m$.
